paper.title: SUBSTANTIAL ANGULAR DEPENDENCE OF THE ELECTRON ENERGY SPECTRA FOR ATTRACTIVE PENNING IONIZATION SYSTEMS: He(2^3S, 2^1S)+Li(2^2S)
affiliations: Fachbereich Physik der Universität, D-6750 Kaiserslautern, Federal Republic of Germany
Fachbereich Chemie der Universität, D-6750 Kaiserslautern, Federal Republic of Germany

research.topic: High-resolution angular-dependent electron spectrometric studies and ab initio quantum mechanical calculations of Penning ionization systems He(2^3S, 2^1S)+Li(2^2S)
objectives: Demonstrate importance of electron angular distribution effects on spectra of attractive Penning ionization systems (well depth D_e > average collision energy E_rel)
Discuss influence of rotational energy exchange between emitted electron and quasi-molecule
Determine potential well depths D_e and semiempirical autoionization width functions from electron spectra

theory.framework: Ab initio quantum mechanical calculations of electron spectra using local functions V_i(R), V_+(R), Γ(R)
approximations: Previous calculations assumed ΔJ = 0 (no rotational energy change during electron emission)
Current work includes rotational energy transfer ΔJ ≠ 0
Classical model for rotational transfer used when partial widths Γ_l unavailable
Semiclassical evaluation of well depth from low-energy edge of Airy peak (44% intensity point)
key_equations: Penning ionization reaction: A* + X → (A + X+) + e- (Eq. 1)
Classical electron energy function: t(R) = V_i(R) - V_+(R) (Eq. 2)
Effective electron energy function with rotational transfer: t(R; ΔJ, J*) = p(R) - V_+(R) - (ħ^2/2μR^2)[ΔJ(2J*+1+ΔJ)] (Eq. 3)
Angular momentum carried by electron: l = [m_Li/(m_Li+m_He)] R p_e sin γ (Eq. 4)
calculations: Classical trajectories at E_rel = 100 meV using real potential V_i(R)
Opacities (ionization probabilities) nearly constant for J* < 80 (~0.73)
Contributions from J* ranges 41-60 and 61-80 to total ionization cross section

numerical.angular_resolution: Limited by velocity distribution variation (20° FWHM)

well_depth_indicator.description: 44% intensity point of main Airy peak

Doppler_shift.value: -15 meV for θ=90° spectrum in apparatus II

key_findings: Substantial angular dependence of electron spectra for attractive Penning systems (He*+Li), not previously reported

For He(2^3S)+Li: (i) Energy shifts of Airy interference structure to higher electron energy with decreasing θ; (ii) Differences in clarity of structure; (iii) Relative increase in plateau intensity at higher energies with decreasing θ
For He(2^1S)+Li: Similar variations but reduced magnitude
Angle-integrated spectrum (apparatus II) shows less structure than θ=90° spectrum (apparatus I) due to angular averaging
Good agreement between ab initio ΔJ=0 calculation and θ=90° experiment supports previous view, but only because rotational energy change influence is small at θ=90°
Inclusion of ΔJ ≠ 0 explains broadening and shifts of interference structures
Classical trajectory calculations reveal preferred orientation of ionizing quasi-molecule leading to angle-dependent rotational transfers
Systematic errors in well depth extraction: E_0.44 varies with angle; best to use θ=90° spectra with detection perpendicular to beam plane to minimize Doppler shifts

fig1.description: Illustration of experimental method to measure Penning ionization electron energy spectra for different ejection angles θ using selected ranges Δφ of cylindrical mirror analyzer (apparatus II)
fig1.content: Geometry of crossed beams and electron detection

fig2.description: Ab initio potential energy curves for He(2^3S, 2^1S)+Li(2^2S) and He(1^1S)+Li+(1^1S) and corresponding Penning ionization electron energy spectra from ref [7] (apparatus I, θ=90°)
fig2.content: Potential curves V_i(R), V_+(R); experimental spectra (bars); theoretical spectrum (smooth line) for He(2^1S)+Li with ΔJ=0 assumption

fig3.description: Electron energy spectra for He(2^3S)+Li and He(2^1S)+Li measured with apparatus II using full azimuthal range (a) and selected Δφ ranges (b,c,d) corresponding to θ = 45°, 90°, 135°
fig3.content: Substantial angular variations in spectral shapes; background subtracted; ordinate scaled to equal main peak height

fig4.description: Comparison of theoretical spectra for He(2^1S)+Li assuming pure ΔJ = -4 (a), ΔJ = 0 (b), ΔJ = +4 (c) transitions
fig4.content: Variations similar to experimental data; peak shifts, plateau increase, stronger modulation for ΔJ = -4

fig5.description: (a) Classical trajectories for He(2^3S)+Li at E_rel=100 meV using real potential V_i(R); (b) Composition of theoretical He(2^3S)+Li electron energy spectrum from separate J* contributions
fig5.content: Trajectories show preferred orientation of ionizing quasi-molecules; J* ranges 41-60 and 61-80 contribute 31% and 43% to cross section

eq3.latex: t(R; \Delta J, J^*) = p(R) - V_+(R) + \frac{\hbar^2}{2\mu R^2}\left[J^*(J^*+1) - (J^*+\Delta J)(J^*+\Delta J+1)\right] = p(R) - V_+(R) - \frac{\hbar^2}{2\mu R^2}\left[\Delta J(2J^*+1+\Delta J)\right]
eq3.description: Effective classical electron energy function including rotational energy transfer

eq4.description: Angular momentum carried away by electron emitted at angle γ relative to internuclear axis

theoretical: Previous calculations neglected rotational energy transfer (ΔJ=0)
Partial widths Γ_l for non-spherical partial waves not available for quantitative treatment
Full account requires more complete theoretical treatment including coupling between electron and nuclear motion
experimental: Angular resolution limited by velocity distribution variation (20° FWHM)
Doppler shifts from center-of-mass motion (corrected -15 meV for θ=90°)
Background subtraction (5-20% of main peak intensity)
interpretation: Classical model used for rotational transfer mechanism
Quantitative treatment of ΔJ ≠ 0 transitions requires partial widths
Measurements at θ=0° and 180° desirable for further clarification
